nodes.description: Global knockout mice reproduce complex IV biochemical impairment and mild workload-dependent diastolic dysfunction. Bulk heart and skeletal-muscle ATP remain preserved. Skeletal muscle shifts toward oxidative fibers with increased isolated fatigue resistance, while uphill exercise performance decreases. Cortical PV cells have oxidative damage, reduced nets and impaired dendritic and fast-spiking maturation, without loss of PV-cell density. Female behavioral cohorts show locomotor hyperactivity with preserved social preference and prepulse inhibition; these are not human psychiatric diagnoses.

nodes.description: Complex IV activity is selectively reduced in patient skeletal muscle. COX6A2 supports the multimeric oxidase and is not itself the electron-transfer catalytic center.
